limitations: Only one underlying policy case; paired scenarios are not independent samples.
LOW and HIGH differ in length as well as cross-record complexity: complexity is not causally isolated.
R0 official conditional-answer Gold is distinct and excluded from synthetic decision accuracy.

No guarantee stronger model will differ across pipelines; 3 repeats measure within-item variation only.
A (three calls) versus B (one call) confounds IR with inference budget; interpret as full-workflow comparison.
Model website Claude repetitions do not expose reproducible random seed; record actual product/model/settings.
Thinking is OFF in the main matrix for both models; a thinking-ON arm is a separate control and must be reported separately.
Strong model is to be called through the API with fixed model ID; temperature/seed controllability under that API must be confirmed in a smoke test.
R0 (official conditional answers) is reported separately from R1-R3 decision-label accuracy and its semantic review is manual.

Stage-wise semantic scores for all runs come from an LLM judge that is valid only after calibration against human labels on a stratified sample (judge_review.py agreement, pre-registered threshold); human-confirmed and judge-labelled numbers are reported apart; human-human agreement has not been measured.

A1 judge fields (coverage, atom_assessment, logic/scope assessment, confidence) come from the user's standalone A1 judge design merged into the stage-wise framework; the judge has never been called live and no human calibration labels exist yet, so every judge-derived number is UNCALIBRATED. A1 for R0 against the official native condition text is still manual.
